title: Projective simplicial-presheaf model structure and its generators
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and the model-category, cofibrant and fibrant conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. A simplicial model category is enriched over simplicial sets with tensors and cotensors as in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor]; for every cofibration $i:A\to B$ and fibration $p:X\to Y$, the induced map $\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$ is a Kan fibration, trivial if $i$ or $p$ is a weak equivalence. The Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] is left proper, combinatorial, and simplicial for its usual Cartesian enrichment. Here left proper means that pushing out a weak equivalence along a cofibration preserves weak equivalences; combinatorial means locally presentable with small generating sets for the two weak factorization systems, and locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, for a regular $\kappa$, by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve these colimits.

For every small ordinary category $D$, the category $\mathsf U(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ has a functorial left proper combinatorial simplicial projective model structure with objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and objectwise Kan fibrations. Its cofibrations have the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial fibrations and are objectwise monomorphisms. Generating cofibrations and generating trivial cofibrations are respectively
$$h_d\times\partial\Delta^n\longrightarrow h_d\times\Delta^n,\qquad h_d\times\Lambda_i^n\longrightarrow h_d\times\Delta^n,$$
where $h_d(e)=\operatorname{Hom}_D(e,d)$ is regarded as a discrete simplicial set, $n\geq0$ in the first family and $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$ in the second. Its tensor and cotensor by a simplicial set are objectwise; its enriched mapping simplicial set has $n$-simplices the natural maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. Its fibrant objects are exactly the presheaves of Kan complexes. No finiteness or nonemptiness condition on $D$ is imposed.

source.place: Example A.3.2.18 and Remark A.3.2.17 (printed p. 863); Proposition A.2.8.2 and Remarks A.2.8.4-A.2.8.5 (pp. 830-832); Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remarks A.3.3.4-A.3.3.5 (pp. 870-871). Left properness follows by the objectwise cofibration and pushout descriptions. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] first with $C=\Delta$, $\mathcal A=\mathsf{Set}$, and then with $C=D$, $\mathcal A=\mathsf{sSet}$. This gives local presentability of simplicial sets and of $\mathsf U(D)$. Simplicial sets have pullbacks and all small limits and colimits by taking the corresponding sets in every simplicial degree; the simplicial operators are induced by the universal properties. The same objectwise construction gives all small limits and colimits of $\mathsf U(D)$. It works for every small $D$, including the empty category.

source.place: Proposition A.2.8.2: local presentability input; Mathlib Presentable/Presheaf.lean:90-96 and Presentable/Type.lean:166-167 supply the cited local presentability theorem. Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], the Kan model structure has monomorphism cofibrations, the boundary generating cofibrations and horn generating trivial cofibrations, and Kan complexes as fibrant objects. Every object is cofibrant since $\varnothing\to X$ is degreewise injective. For a monomorphism $i:A\to B$ and weak equivalence $w:A\to A^{\prime}$, apply the pushout clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] to the spans $(B\leftarrow A\xrightarrow{1}A)$ and $(B\leftarrow A\xrightarrow{w}A^{\prime})$, with components $(1_B,1_A,w)$. Both designated maps $A\to B$ are $i$, hence monomorphisms. Their pushouts are $B$ and $B\amalg_A A^{\prime}$, so the induced map is a weak equivalence. This is left properness. Together with Step 1 and the two small generating families, this proves combinatoriality. For the Cartesian enrichment put $\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(X\times\Delta^n,Y)$, tensor $X\times K$ and cotensor $Y^K$, where $(Y^K)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(K\times\Delta^n,Y)$ and simplicial operators act by precomposition. The adjunction is explicit: a map $X\times K\to Y$ sends a simplex $x:\Delta^n\to X$ to the composite $\Delta^n\times K\to X\times K\to Y$; the inverse evaluates this family on the identity simplex, and naturality makes the two formulas inverse. For monomorphisms $i,j$, their pushout product is the inclusion of the union of $B\times C$ and $A\times E$ in $B\times E$, hence is monic. If either factor is trivial, it is anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product], using symmetry when necessary; anodyne equals trivial cofibration by the Kan lifting system. Exponential adjunction identifies a horn lifting problem for the mapping-space map associated to $i,p$ with a lifting problem for $i\mathbin\square(\Lambda_k^n\to\Delta^n)$ against $p$, and identifies boundary lifting similarly. The pushout-product conclusions therefore give exactly the simplicial model axiom, including both triviality alternatives.

proof.text: For each $d\in D$ define $L_d(K)(e)=\coprod_{\alpha:e\to d}K=h_d(e)\times K$, with restriction along $\beta:e^{\prime}\to e$ sending $(\alpha,x)$ to $(\alpha\beta,x)$. Evaluation at the identity of $d$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(L_dK,F)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,F(d))$: its inverse sends $x:K\to F(d)$ to $(\alpha,k)\mapsto F(\alpha)(x(k))$. The two formulas are inverse by naturality at $\alpha$ and at $1_d$. Thus $L_d$ is left adjoint to evaluation, and lifting squares correspond under these same formulas. Let $I_D$ and $J_D$ be $L_d$ applied to all boundary and horn inclusions with the ranges in the statement. These are small sets since $D$ is small. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $I_D^{\square}$ is exactly the objectwise trivial fibrations and $J_D^{\square}$ exactly the objectwise Kan fibrations.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.8.2, free-diagram formula and identification of the two right lifting classes. Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: Run the cellular small object argument separately on $I_D$ and $J_D$. Its smallness hypothesis is justified as follows. By Step 1 and [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank], each domain of a generator has a regular presentability rank. The domains form a small family. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the underlying sets of these rank cardinals and choose an infinite regular $\lambda$ greater than all of them. The initial ordinal of $\lambda$ is filtered for every smaller rank, so the Hom functor of each domain preserves every continuous $\lambda$-chain, in particular chains of generator-cell attachments. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] now hold. It gives functorial factorizations into an $I_D$-cell map followed by an objectwise trivial fibration, and into a $J_D$-cell map followed by an objectwise fibration. It also identifies each generated left lifting class with the arrow retracts of the corresponding cell maps.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.8.2, the two small-object factorizations; cited cardinal and cellular lemmas discharge the smallness hypothesis. Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: Define weak equivalences objectwise, fibrations as $J_D^{\square}$, and cofibrations as ${}^{\square}(I_D^{\square})$. Evaluation preserves colimits by their explicit objectwise construction. An evaluated $I_D$ generator is a coproduct of boundary inclusions, so every $I_D$-cell map is objectwise monic, as are its arrow retracts. An evaluated $J_D$ generator is a coproduct of trivial Kan cofibrations. A cell composite built from these has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration: solve a square at each attached summand, extend the chosen diagonal at successor stages, and use the colimit universal property at limit stages. Retracts inherit the diagonal by composing the retract maps. Hence every $J_D$-cell map is an objectwise trivial cofibration, in particular a weak equivalence, and is a projective cofibration since its generators lift against objectwise trivial fibrations. Conversely, if a projective cofibration $f$ is an objectwise weak equivalence, factor $f=pj$ by the $J_D$ factorization of Step 4. Both $j$ and $f$ are objectwise weak equivalences, so $p$ is an objectwise trivial fibration. A lift against $p$ makes $f$ an arrow retract of $j$ (the retract has identity on the source and the diagonal on the target). Therefore the second generated left class is precisely the trivial projective cofibrations. The two weak factorization systems now satisfy all the model axioms: retract and two-out-of-three for weak equivalences are componentwise, and completeness, cocompleteness and functorial factorizations were proved above. This also proves exactly the asserted two generating families, objectwise monomorphism property, and combinatoriality.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.8.2, the lifting/retract argument; Remark A.2.8.5, projective cofibrations are objectwise cofibrations. Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: Regard $J=D^{\mathrm{op}}$ as the small simplicial category $I$ with discrete mapping sets $I(d,e)=\operatorname{Hom}_J(d,e)$ and composition induced from $J$. Enriched functors $I\to\mathrm{sSet}$ are exactly ordinary $J$-diagrams: a map out of a discrete mapping set chooses one ordinary arrow for each $\alpha$, and the unit and composition equations are the functor laws. Enriched naturality is ordinary naturality at each $\alpha$. Apply [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation] with $\mathcal A=\mathrm{sSet}$, locally presentable by Step 1 and enriched, tensored and cotensored by Step 2. It supplies the diagram enrichment, its mapping end, and objectwise tensor and cotensor. Thus $(F\otimes K)(d)=F(d)\times K$, $(G^K)(d)=G(d)^K$, and $\operatorname{Map}(F,G)_n=\operatorname{Nat}(F\times\Delta^n,G)$. The operators act by precomposition and composition uses the diagonal, as in the Cartesian enrichment. The tensor/cotensor conventions [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] make these representing data with enriched natural isomorphisms $\operatorname{Map}(F\otimes K,G)\cong[K,\operatorname{Map}(F,G)]\cong\operatorname{Map}(F,G^K)$. On vertices they give both parametrized adjunctions used below. No model-compatibility conclusion is taken from the diagram lemma.

proof.text: Let $i:A\to B$ be a projective cofibration, $j:K\to L$ a simplicial monomorphism and $p:X\to Y$ an objectwise Kan fibration. Put $q_j(p):X^L\to X^K\times_{Y^K}Y^L$. At $d$ this is $\operatorname{Map}(L,X(d))\to\operatorname{Map}(K,X(d))\times_{\operatorname{Map}(K,Y(d))}\operatorname{Map}(L,Y(d))$, since cotensors and pullbacks are objectwise. Step 2 therefore makes $q_j(p)$ an objectwise Kan fibration, and an objectwise trivial fibration if $j$ is a weak equivalence or $p$ is objectwise trivial. This uses the Kan simplicial axiom only at a single object, with the cofibration $j$ and the fibration $p(d)$.

source.place: Remark A.3.3.4 and Remark A.3.1.6, enriched model compatibility; verified here by the tensor/cotensor adjunction against the objectwise cotensor maps (repair by the maintainer reader). Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-parametrized-adjunction-corner-lifting] to the adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}(F\otimes K,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,G^K)$ supplied by [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation]. It identifies $\operatorname{LLP}(i\mathbin\square j,p)$ with $\operatorname{LLP}(i,q_j(p))$, where $i\mathbin\square j:(A\otimes L)\amalg_{A\otimes K}(B\otimes K)\to B\otimes L$. When $p$ is objectwise trivial, the preceding step makes $q_j(p)$ objectwise trivial. The defining lifting property of $i$ gives the required lift. Thus $i\mathbin\square j$ lifts against all objectwise trivial fibrations, so is a projective cofibration by Step 5.

source.place: Remark A.3.3.4 and Remark A.3.1.6, enriched model compatibility; verified here by the tensor/cotensor adjunction against the objectwise cotensor maps (repair by the maintainer reader). Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: If $j$ is also a weak equivalence, the same corner-lifting equivalence [lem-coef-parametrized-adjunction-corner-lifting] makes $i\mathbin\square j$ lift against every projective fibration: the preceding objectwise computation makes $q_j(p)$ trivial for every such $p$, and $i$ lifts against it. If $i$ is instead a trivial projective cofibration, $q_j(p)$ is a projective fibration for every projective fibration $p$, and $i$ lifts against it by Step 5. In either case $i\mathbin\square j$ belongs to the left class of the second weak factorization system of Step 5, hence is a trivial projective cofibration.

source.place: Remark A.3.3.4 and Remark A.3.1.6, enriched model compatibility; verified here by the tensor/cotensor adjunction against the objectwise cotensor maps (repair by the maintainer reader). Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-parametrized-adjunction-corner-lifting] a second time, now for $\operatorname{Hom}(F\otimes K,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,\operatorname{Map}(F,G))$ from [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation]. For a projective cofibration $i:A\to B$ and projective fibration $p:X\to Y$, lifting a simplicial map $j$ against $r:\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$ is equivalent to lifting $i\mathbin\square j$ against $p$. For a horn inclusion $j$, this pushout product is trivial by the preceding step, so all horn lifts exist. If $p$ is trivial, every boundary inclusion gives a cofibration pushout product by the earlier corner calculation, so it lifts against $p$. If $i$ is trivial, each boundary pushout product is trivial and lifts against $p$. The horn and boundary characterizations in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], including the zero-dimensional boundary, show that $r$ is a Kan fibration, trivial in both asserted cases. This proves the required simplicial model axiom with the stated enrichment.

source.place: Remark A.3.3.4 and Remark A.3.1.6, enriched model compatibility; verified here by the tensor/cotensor adjunction against the objectwise cotensor maps (repair by the maintainer reader). Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: A pushout along a projective cofibration is objectwise a pushout along a Kan cofibration, by Step 5. The Kan structure is left proper by Step 2, so pushing out an objectwise weak equivalence preserves objectwise weak equivalences. Thus the projective structure is left proper. Finally, its terminal diagram is objectwise the terminal simplicial set. Its terminal map is a projective fibration exactly when every component terminal map is a Kan fibration, that is, when every component is a Kan complex by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For empty $D$ there is one diagram and one arrow, and the empty generating families yield the terminal model category. No step required finite $D$ or a chosen object of $D$.
